stories.title: Alzheimer’s may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss
stories.summary: Johns Hopkins scientists have uncovered hidden warning signs of Alzheimer’s disease that may appear up to a decade before memory loss begins. Brain scans revealed that two regions involved in memory and emotion start shrinking before the hippocampus, the area doctors typically examine for signs of Alzheimer’s. These early changes are linked to abnormal tau protein buildup and could provide a powerful new way to identify people at risk.

stories.title: Scientists discover a bizarre paradox among endangered penguins
stories.summary: A groundbreaking drone survey has revealed a startling split in the fate of New Zealand's endangered Erect-crested penguins. While one population has remained stable for decades, another has declined by more than 40%, apparently due to a combination of predators, worsening storms, and changing ocean conditions. Even more surprisingly, the tiny Bounty Islands support nearly as many breeding pairs as the Antipodes Islands, despite being 40 times smaller.

Split the cards into two piles: face cards plus aces, and the numbered cards. Shuffle both. The card drawn sets the distance, the direction, and the slope. Numbered cards show the feet for the putt.
